_readme: Mock Salesforce data for sf-case-copilot. Field names match real Salesforce API names so Step 6 can swap this file for a live org with minimal code change. Cases use standard Case fields. Articles use Knowledge__kav fields, where Answer__c is a custom rich-text field (Salesforce ships Knowledge__kav with Title/Summary/UrlName and expects you to add your own body field). NOTE: in a real org Answer__c contains HTML, not plain text -- Step 6 will need to strip tags.

cases.Subject: Cannot log in to Community portal after password reset
cases.Description: Customer reset their password via the 'Forgot Password' link on our Experience Cloud site. They received the reset email and set a new password, but logging in still returns 'Your login attempt has failed.' They have tried two different browsers. Account was created 3 weeks ago.

cases.Subject: Report shows no rows for records the user can see in list view
cases.Description: A sales user can open Opportunity records directly and sees them in a list view, but a custom report of the same object returns zero rows for them. Other users on the same profile see the expected rows. Report was working for this user last month.

cases.Subject: Duplicate Account records created after Data Loader import
cases.Description: We imported 4,200 Accounts using Data Loader last night. Roughly 900 of them already existed and are now duplicated. Duplicate rules are active on Account but did not block the insert. We need to understand why and how to clean this up safely.

cases.Subject: Integration failing with REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
cases.Description: Our middleware started receiving REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED from the REST API around 14:00 yesterday and has been failing intermittently since. Nothing changed on our side. We sync roughly 60,000 Contact records per day across several jobs.

cases.Subject: Customer emails are not creating Cases anymore
cases.Description: Emails sent to support@ourcompany-example.com used to create Cases automatically. Since Monday nothing arrives in Salesforce, though senders do not get a bounce message. We use Email-to-Case. No changes were made to the routing address that we are aware of.

cases.Subject: Partner user gets 'login attempt has failed' only from the office
cases.Description: One partner user can log in to our Experience Cloud site from home without problems, but always fails from their office network. Same username and password. Other users at the same partner company are not affected.

cases.Subject: Dashboard totals differ depending on who opens it
cases.Description: Our regional dashboard shows 1.2M in pipeline for the VP but only 340K for a sales manager who should see the same territory. The underlying report uses a standard Opportunity report type with no owner filter. Is this expected behaviour?

cases.Subject: Data Loader upsert fails with INVALID_FIELD_FOR_INSERT_UPDATE
cases.Description: Trying to upsert Contacts against our External_Id__c field. Data Loader errors on every row with INVALID_FIELD_FOR_INSERT_UPDATE. The field exists and is populated in our CSV. We successfully ran the same file structure in sandbox last quarter.

cases.Subject: Nightly sync is slow and occasionally hits governor limits
cases.Description: Our nightly Contact sync takes over 4 hours and sometimes fails partway with limit errors. We currently send records one at a time through the REST API. Looking for guidance on the right approach for this volume before our next data migration.

cases.Subject: Custom Lightning component renders incorrectly on iPad
cases.Description: Our custom LWC quote builder displays with overlapping columns on iPad Safari in the Salesforce mobile app. It looks correct on desktop Chrome and on iPhone. The component uses a CSS grid layout inside a lightning-card.

knowledge_articles.Title: Troubleshooting Experience Cloud Login Failures
knowledge_articles.Summary: Why a Community or Partner user sees 'Your login attempt has failed' even with a correct password, and how to find the real cause in Login History.
knowledge_articles.Answer__c:
The message 'Your login attempt has failed' is deliberately generic and does not mean the password is wrong. Work through these checks:

1. Check Login History first. Setup > Identity > Login History, filter by the username. The Status column gives the true reason: 'Invalid Password', 'Restricted IP', 'Frozen User', 'User is inactive', or 'Password Lockout'. This single step usually identifies the cause and saves the rest of the list.

2. Confirm the user record is active. Setup > Users. The user must be Active and not Frozen. A deactivated Contact's user record produces this exact error.

3. Confirm the Contact and Account are valid. A Community user cannot log in if the parent Contact is inactive, or if the parent Account has no active owner.

4. Verify site membership. Digital Experiences > All Sites > [Site] > Administration > Members. The user's Profile must be listed as a member of that specific site. A profile removed from Members blocks every user assigned to it.

5. Check Login IP Ranges and Login Hours on the Profile. Login IP Ranges are enforced strictly: a user who succeeds from home and fails from the office almost always has an office IP outside the permitted range. Login Hours are evaluated in the org's default time zone, not the user's.

6. Confirm the site itself is Active, not in Preview. A site left in Preview only admits users with 'View Setup and Configuration'.

If Login History shows no entry at all for the attempt, the request is not reaching the org: check that the user is using the site's login URL rather than login.salesforce.com.

knowledge_articles.Title: Records Missing from Reports but Visible in List Views
knowledge_articles.Summary: Why a report returns fewer rows than a user expects, covering report filters, report types, role hierarchy and field-level security.
knowledge_articles.Answer__c:
When a user can open records directly but a report returns nothing, record access is usually fine and the report itself is filtering the rows out.

1. Check the 'Show Me' filter. Set to 'My opportunities' or 'My team's opportunities' it silently scopes results to the running user. Switch to 'All opportunities' to test.

2. Check the standard date filter. The Date Field, Range and fiscal year settings apply on every run. The user's Locale and Time Zone shift range boundaries, so two users can get different rows from the same saved report.

3. Check the report type. A 'with' report type (for example 'Opportunities with Products') is an inner join and excludes any parent record lacking a child. Switching to a 'with or without' report type is the fix.

4. Check the role hierarchy. Reports respect sharing. Two users on the same Profile but at different points in the role hierarchy see different rows, because Profile controls object permissions while Role controls record visibility. This is the usual explanation when a VP and a manager see different dashboard totals.

5. Check Field-Level Security on filter fields. If a field used in a filter is hidden for the user's profile, the filter cannot evaluate and rows drop out silently.

6. Check filter logic and cross filters in report Edit mode. Cross filters ('without Activities') exclude records in ways that are not visible on the run page.

Remember that dashboards run as a specified running user by default. If a dashboard shows the same numbers to everyone, or different numbers than the source report, check the dashboard's running-user setting before investigating sharing.

knowledge_articles.Title: Preventing and Resolving Duplicates in Data Loader Imports
knowledge_articles.Summary: Why duplicate rules do not block Data Loader inserts, and how to use External IDs and upsert to make imports repeatable.
knowledge_articles.Answer__c:
Duplicate Rules do not reliably block records inserted through the API. By design, a Duplicate Rule's action for API operations is configurable, and the default 'Allow' setting merely reports the duplicate rather than preventing it. Data Loader is an API client, so an active rule that blocks duplicates in the UI can still allow thousands through an import.

To prevent duplicates:

1. Set the Duplicate Rule's Alert action to Block explicitly, and confirm 'Alert' and 'Report' are enabled for the API operation, not just for the UI.

2. Better, use an External ID field and upsert instead of insert. Mark a field as External ID and Unique on the object, populate it in your source system, and run Data Loader in Upsert mode against that field. Upsert matches on the External ID: existing records update, new ones insert. This makes the import idempotent, so re-running the same file is safe.

3. Confirm the matching rule the duplicate rule references is active. A duplicate rule pointing at an inactive matching rule never matches anything.

Common upsert errors:

- INVALID_FIELD_FOR_INSERT_UPDATE when upserting usually means the chosen field is not actually marked as an External ID in the target org, or the CSV column header does not match the field's API name exactly (including the __c suffix). Sandbox and production can differ here: a field marked External ID in sandbox is not automatically so in production after deployment.

- DUPLICATE_VALUE means the External ID is not unique in your source file. De-duplicate the CSV before loading.

To clean up existing duplicates, use Duplicate Record Sets and the Merge Duplicates feature rather than deleting rows, so that child records are reparented instead of orphaned.

knowledge_articles.Title: Handling REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and API Request Limits
knowledge_articles.Summary: How the 24-hour rolling API limit works, how to see current consumption, and which API to use for bulk volumes.
knowledge_articles.Answer__c:
REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED means the org has exhausted its allocation of API calls for the trailing 24 hours. The limit is a rolling window, not a midnight reset, so an org can recover gradually without any change on your side. This is why the error often appears intermittent.

To diagnose:

1. Check current consumption. Setup > Company Information shows 'API Requests, Last 24 Hours' with the current count and maximum. The System Overview page shows the same figure.

2. Identify the caller. Setup > API Usage Notifications can be configured to alert at a threshold. The Event Monitoring ApiEvent or the Setup Audit Trail help identify which integration user is consuming the allocation.

3. Look for a change in call pattern rather than a change in volume. An integration that switches from bulk to single-record calls will multiply its request count without moving more data.

To reduce consumption:

- Use the Bulk API 2.0 for anything above a few thousand records. Bulk API batches consume dramatically fewer request units than one REST call per record: 60,000 records sent individually is 60,000 requests, while the same data through Bulk API 2.0 is a small number of job requests.

- Use Composite and sObject Collections endpoints for medium volumes. A composite request can carry up to 25 subrequests and counts as one API call. sObject Collections handles up to 200 records per call.

- Query with SOQL rather than looping. Retrieving 200 records with one query is one request; retrieving them individually is 200.

- Cache reference data such as picklist metadata rather than re-requesting it on every run.

For a genuine sustained increase, additional API capacity can be purchased, but review the call pattern first: the overwhelming majority of these cases are resolved by moving to Bulk API 2.0.

knowledge_articles.Title: Email-to-Case Messages Not Creating Cases
knowledge_articles.Summary: Checks for when inbound support email stops producing Cases, including routing address verification, daily limits and forwarding configuration.
knowledge_articles.Answer__c:
When inbound mail stops creating Cases and senders receive no bounce, the mail is usually being accepted and then discarded by the email service.

1. Check the routing address verification status. Setup > Email-to-Case > Routing Addresses. Each address has a verification status; a routing address whose verification has lapsed silently stops creating Cases. Re-send the verification email and confirm it.

2. Check the daily email service limit. On-Demand Email-to-Case processes a limited number of messages per day, calculated as 1,000 multiplied by the number of user licences. Messages beyond the limit are discarded or bounced depending on the email service's failure response setting. Setup > Email Services shows the failure response configuration.

3. Check the email service's error handling. If 'Route Error Messages to' is unset, failures are silent. Set it to a monitored address so future problems surface.

4. Confirm the forwarding rule at your mail provider still exists. Email-to-Case depends on your mail server forwarding to a Salesforce-generated address. Mail platform migrations and security policy changes frequently drop these forwarding rules. Send a test message directly to the Salesforce-generated address: if that creates a Case, the problem is in your mail provider, not in Salesforce.

5. Check for attachment size and content restrictions. Messages exceeding the size limit are rejected as a whole.

6. Confirm the Case assignment rule is active. A message that creates a Case which is then assigned to an inactive queue owner can appear to have vanished. Search Cases by the sender's address before concluding nothing was created.
